exception_policy: exceptions require explicit documented technical justification

commandments.title: Thou shalt not write bloat
commandments.rule: prefer the smallest clear implementation that satisfies the declared contract; remove ornamental abstraction and duplicated machinery

commandments.title: Thou shalt not hide state
commandments.rule: inputs outputs mutable state configuration caches and side effects must be explicit and inspectable

commandments.title: Thou shalt not confuse projection with source
commandments.rule: derived artifacts must remain distinguishable from canonical source and reproducible from it where claimed

commandments.title: Thou shalt not summon needless dependencies
commandments.rule: do not add a dependency when a small clear well-tested implementation is safer and simpler; security and correctness override dependency-count vanity

commandments.title: Thou shalt fail loudly and usefully
commandments.rule: fail closed where required; errors must identify what failed and what evidence or input is missing

commandments.title: Thou shalt make determinism explicit
commandments.rule: deterministic claims must declare inputs runtime canonicalization ambient-state exclusions and output scope

commandments.title: Thou shalt preserve provenance
commandments.rule: every imported specimen or context slice must retain source identity license epistemic class and canonical status

commandments.title: Thou shalt not worship the network
commandments.rule: core verification and recovery should work offline where practical; network dependencies must be necessary explicit and replaceable

commandments.title: Thou shalt keep machine truth inspectable
commandments.rule: machine-readable contracts must remain reviewable with ordinary tools and must not depend on opaque latent state as sole authority

commandments.title: Thou shalt leave it simpler
commandments.rule: changes should reduce accidental complexity or clearly justify any complexity they add
